pairs.question: Syllane, quo te proripis?
pairs.derivation: Vitellius asks Syllanus whither he is rushing; Syllanus answers 'straight to the senate.' The speaker-labels (VITELL., SYL.) and verse line-break are stripped. The reply opens with the vocative address 'censor gravis,' (addressing Vitellius) which is framing/address, not the answer; the operative answering words are 'recta in senatum.'

pairs.question: cur non licet?
pairs.derivation: Vitellius has just said 'non licet'; Syllanus asks 'why is it not allowed?'; Vitellius answers 'I am removing you from the senate.' Speaker-labels stripped. Answer stops at the full stop before Syllanus's next retort.

pairs.question: scelus ipsa dicis?
pairs.derivation: Pallas asks Agrippina 'do you yourself call it a crime?'; she answers affirmatively 'I admit it, and a great crime.' Real yes/no interrogative genuinely answered. Speaker-labels and verse line-break stripped.

pairs.question: perimes maritum?
pairs.derivation: Pallas asks 'will you kill your husband?'; Agrippina answers affirmatively 'indeed, lest he kill, he dies.' Speaker-labels and trailing verse-number 470 / line-break stripped.

pairs.question: perit imperator?
pairs.derivation: Pallas asks 'does the emperor die?'; Agrippina answers 'indeed, so that I may enjoy the empire.' Speaker-labels and verse line-break stripped.

pairs.question: lento, an cito?
pairs.derivation: In the interrogation about how Claudius is to be poisoned, Pallas asks 'by slow or quick [poison]?'; Agrippina answers that a hasty deed is betrayed, treachery is by the slow one (i.e. slow poison). Answer cut at the first full stop; what follows ('inde odia nobis...') elaborates her motive. The preceding 'quo genere mortis' exchange was dropped as the source word is garbled with injected spaces ('quo ge    nere').

pairs.question: quaenam artifex?
pairs.derivation: Pallas asks 'who is the [poisoning] artificer?'; Agrippina answers 'Locusta, already accused of crime.' Speaker-labels and verse line-break stripped.

pairs.question: et quis minister?
pairs.derivation: Pallas asks 'and who the agent?'; Agrippina answers 'Ganymede himself, the eunuch Halotus.' Answer is verbatim across the two verse lines (899-900); speaker-labels stripped.

pairs.question: haec quo?
pairs.derivation: Pallas asks 'to what end these things?'; Agrippina answers 'so that my son may reign.' Speaker-labels and trailing verse-number 490 / line-break stripped.

pairs.question: regnabit Nero?
pairs.answer: regnabit; at si regnet, in matrem ruet.
pairs.derivation: Agrippina asks the augur Agerinus 'will Nero reign?'; he first deflects ('tacere liceat', a non-answering preamble dropped), then when pressed answers 'He will reign; but if he reigns, he will rush upon his mother.' The framing imperative 'loquere' ('speak!') is dropped as it narrates the asking, not the question itself.

pairs.question: Narcisse, nosti, noster an vivat pater?
pairs.derivation: Britannicus asks Narcissus whether their father still lives; Narcissus answers 'he lives, but ill.' Speaker-labels and verse line-break stripped; answer cut at the full stop before Britannicus's next line.
